description: Rave scenes per host faction: the venue picture (an 'illustrations' key from settings.json), the arrival scene shown above the first conversation at each rave, and crowd lines (one per rave conversation, from the faction's list plus default's). 'arrival' is either one text or one per Rave Licensing level: anything_goes, permissive, licensed, strict, banned; missing levels fall back to default. Another mod can add its faction in its own copy of this file. See docs/immersion-audit/RAVE_IDEAS.md.

default.arrival: You step through the hatch into a cargo hold stripped to the bulkheads, and the bass hits you in the sternum before your eyes adjust. Strobes catch a crowd in rolled-up uniform sleeves. Someone hands you a drink you didn't order. Three bodies away, a captain you last saw down a gun sight is dancing with her eyes shut. Over the door, somebody has taped a hand-lettered sign across the duty roster: OFF SHIFT.
crowd: A dockhand and a commodore are trading dance moves by the speakers, and for once nobody is checking anyone's rank.
A crew in from the frontier cheers every time the bass drops, like it's the first time they've heard music this loud. It might be.
Someone started a chant three songs ago. Half the room still doesn't know the words, and it hasn't slowed anyone down.
A pilot hoists her wingmate onto her shoulders so he can see the lights. He spends the whole song pointing at them.
Two crews who nearly came to blows over a docking slot last week are sharing a table, arguing happily about whose ship is the worst.
The DJ drops an old Domain-era anthem, and a whole corner of the hall sings it back word for word, grinning at each other.
A rating from an engine crew, barely old enough to be here, dances like nobody ever told them how. Nobody does.
Someone has projected a sky from a world most of the room has never seen across the ceiling. People keep looking up and smiling.

arrival.banned: Someone who won't give their name leads you down to a chapel bay. The icons have been turned to face the wall. The music is low and the dancing lower, and every few minutes a figure at the hatch raises a hand and the whole room goes still until the footsteps outside have passed.
arrival.strict: A curate stands at the speaker stacks reading the Litany of Restraint over the opening bars, and the censer smoke is so thick it swallows the lights. The faithful dance in slow, careful rows. Knights stand at the door, and you notice the dancers keep one eye on them, and the Knights keep both eyes on the dancers.
arrival.licensed: A deacon blesses the speakers before the first track. You time it: eleven seconds. Then the bass drops and the faithful sway in hooded rows, while the same deacon walks the edge of the floor with a slate, writing down the names of those who sway too freely.
arrival.permissive: The censers are smoking, and whatever is in them isn't incense. A bishop in full vestments is preaching at the speaker stacks, and the congregation shouts every response on the beat. Near the altar you spot a Knight with his helm under his arm. As you watch, he sets it down on a pew and walks away from it.
arrival.anything_goes: The icons are wearing glowsticks. The choir gave up on hymns an hour ago and now sings over the drops. An archbishop rides a reliquary across the heads of the crowd, blessing everyone he passes with both hands, and when he passes you somebody presses a holy medal and a drink into your palm at the same time. Every preacher you can hear is shouting that this is what Ludd always wanted.

luddic_path.arrival: You smell the smoke before you see the hold. Every speaker in the system seems to have been dragged in here, all of them playing at full volume while Pathers beat them apart with wrenches, in time. The congregation dances on the wreckage. A Brother-Captain stands on a burning synthesizer, preaching, and when two of the faithful start headbutting a subwoofer he blesses them both. The subwoofer is still playing.

sindrian_diktat.arrival: The first thing you see is Andrada: ten metres tall on every screen in the hall, smiling down at the dance floor. The bass is so deep your teeth hum, and a brass plaque by the speaker stacks informs you that it is officially the deepest in human space. Credit chits flutter down from the balconies like snow. Below, Lion's Guard officers catch them without breaking step. Between tracks a voice announces that tonight's playlist was personally approved, and the crowd is cheering before it finishes the sentence.

tritachyon.arrival: A drone checks your credit rating at the door and waves you through. Something gold is running in a channel cut into the bar, and people are drinking it straight from the channel. The light show is doing things you're fairly sure light isn't supposed to do. An executive in a suit worth more than your flagship leans over to tell you the venue was bought this afternoon and will be written off by morning, then vanishes into the crowd before you can ask who it was bought from.

hegemony.arrival: A marine at the hangar door takes your personal recorder, seals it in a bag and writes your name on the bag. Inside, the lights are low, the music is loud, and the room is full of Hegemony officers in dress uniform dancing like nobody is watching, because nobody is allowed to. At the bar a COMSEC lieutenant drinks with one hand and holds a blank incident report in the other. When a camera drone drifts in through a vent, three commodores shoot it down without missing a beat.

pirates.arrival: You hear it two decks before you see it. Then the hatch opens and the heat hits you: a dark hold packed shoulder to shoulder, bass shaking rust out of the ceiling, a man working through the crowd with a rattling bag and a fistful of credits. Half the faces you pass have pupils like reactor cores. On the drop somebody fires a flare at the ceiling, and the whole hold cheers like it has already won.

persean.arrival: Two sound systems face each other across the hall, each draped in a different House's colours, each playing a different track at full volume. In the middle the songs collide into something nobody planned. A pair of Doux in brocade are dancing a duel along the seam between them, and the guests on either side cheer for their own.

HMI.arrival: A clerk at the door of the ore hold scans your ID and stamps your hand with the Company logo. Inside, the deck still smells of slag. Mining drones hang from the ceiling with their cutting lasers dialled down to strobe, and by the door a quarterly bonus is being paid out in cash from a cargo crate, to a queue that is dancing. In the middle of the floor a Director in a pressed suit is doing a frankly alarming impression of a mass driver. Nobody films it.
crowd: A shift crew still in their hardsuits stomps out a rhythm on the deck plates. The DJ considers it for a moment, then builds the next track around it.
Someone has parked a mining tug in the middle of the dance floor and painted the Company logo on it. People are dancing on the roof.
